props.label: Self containment and routing pass
props.html:
Self containment and routing pass

Five changes, all mechanical. No page was redesigned, no approved copy was rewritten, and home-v7.html remains the locked reference for the home page.

RefMeasuredCorrectionPages
V8-01The question list was capped at 900px inside a 1152px content column, so it stopped short of every other block on the page and left an empty band down its right hand side.The cap is gone. The list is a direct child of the content container on all 79 pages that carry one, so it now measures 1152px at 1440 and 354px at 390, the same as the blocks above and below it. Measured on both. No answer was lengthened, shortened or rewritten.79
V8-02184 elements carried a style attribute: a link colour on dark bands (31), the footer's second paragraph spacing (148) and the five positions of the coverage map pins.Three classes and one adjacency selector in the stylesheet, carrying the same values. The footer is reached by its position rather than by a new class, so the approved footer markup is unchanged. Nothing moved and nothing changed colour. The only style attributes left anywhere are the four the before and after sliders write at runtime, which is the slider position and is behaviour rather than markup.148
V8-03Every page loaded site.css and site.js as separate files, so a page on its own was incomplete.The stylesheet is written into one <style> block at the end of each head and the behaviour into one <script> block at the end of each body, in the positions the <link> and <script src> occupied. Both files stay in the folder for the CMS to load globally, and are byte for byte what the pages carry. The one remaining external request is the Google Fonts stylesheet, which the approved typography needs.148
V8-04A standalone /get-a-quote/ page sat in the architecture alongside a Quick Quote panel that did the same job, so some quote buttons opened the panel and others navigated away from the page the visitor was reading.The page is removed. All 596 quote controls across the site now open the panel in the global header: 16 buttons and prose links were repointed, the route map went from 149 routes to 148, and the thank you page's Send Another button opens the panel too, which is the only way a visitor who forgot an attachment can send a second enquiry. The register records the page as dropped rather than deleting the row; it was never on the live site, so no redirect is needed. The panel, the form and the Thank You flow are unchanged, and the full three step form was re-tested through the panel on the page that used to route to the old one.148
V8-05A quote control's href has to point somewhere real, both because an href to nothing is broken markup and because the control should still do something sensible before the script has loaded. Six pages carry no inline quote section for it to point at.On the 142 pages that have one, #quote reaches the inline form, which is a visible fallback. The six that do not point at the panel itself, which is on every page. Every fragment on every page now resolves.148
V8-06The Quick Quote drawer was one component in the global header, but 142 pages also carried a second copy of the three step form in the page body, as an inline quote section. Two places to change meant two places to get wrong, and the home page carried its own hand authored copy of the header and drawer on top of that.The inline quote sections are removed, all 142 of them: 65 came from the shared page closer and 13 from direct calls, and the component that built them is deleted so it cannot come back. The home page now takes the same global header component as every other page instead of its own copy. cms-implementation/global-header.html is the single source for the header, navigation, Quick Quote tab, drawer, form, validation and open and close behaviour, and qa/headerqa.py proves all 148 pages carry it. All 596 quote controls point at #pe-quote-panel and open the drawer in place. The home page hero panel stays, because it is part of the approved design. Section rhythm was re-checked after the removal: no page ends up with two sections of the same surface side by side.148
V8-08The two CMS components still loaded the logo from /uploads/prime-exteriors-logo.png, so a header or footer pasted from cms-implementation/ needed that one file uploaded before it rendered, while every delivered page needed nothing.Both components embed the logo, as the same right sized WebP data URI the pages carry, written by the same encoder from the same file. Neither component references a path for any image. The header check is now a character for character comparison against the component rather than one that ignored image sources, which is a stronger guarantee than before.2
V8-07The thank you page's closing band said Back To Home and pointed at the home page, but it carried the drawer trigger, so it opened the quote panel instead of going home. Introduced when the page stopped stripping that attribute.The band adds the trigger only when its button actually points at the panel. Clicking Back To Home now loads the home page, confirmed in a browser.1

Two QA checks were narrowed, and why

The contrast check read the three step form's later steps, which the script disables until the visitor reaches them, and reported the browser's own grey for a disabled control as 28 failures per page. WCAG 1.4.3 exempts an inactive component, and those steps are inside [hidden] and not painted at all, so they are now skipped. The same check read screen reader only text, which is clipped to a one pixel box and never painted; that is skipped too. Both were masking real findings rather than adding any.

What is left after narrowing: internal pages measure clean, and the home page holds four marginal readings between 4.35 and 4.37 against a 4.5 target, all of them the approved aqua and slate on the sky surface. The darkening that fixed this elsewhere (V6-8) is deliberately scoped to .px-int so the approved home page renders exactly as approved, and the home page is locked.

One measurement that reads as a finding and is not

At 320px the chevron inside Read our Google reviews sits 19px past the button's padded content box. It is still 11px inside the button itself, the button does not scroll (scrollWidth 232 equals clientWidth 232) and nothing is clipped: the label simply uses part of the right hand padding at the narrowest width. Photographed at 320 to be sure.

The global shell

The header, the mega menu and the footer were compared against home-v6.html on all 148 delivered pages, with whitespace normalised and the current-page marker ignored. One character differs, on every page, and it is required.

Whathome-v6DeliveredWhy
Footer logo pathsrc="/uploads/prime-exteriors-logo.png"src="/uploads/prime-exteriors-logo.png"Section 23.8 requires the production path. The relative form resolves only from the folder root.

No navigation item, mega menu entry, footer link, button or interaction was added, removed or restyled. The v6 shell already carried every route in the approved architecture, so nothing needed expanding.

The stylesheet

site.css opens with the home-v6.html stylesheet reproduced verbatim, then appends three commented blocks. Nothing inside the v6 portion is edited, overwritten or reordered.

The first ten corrections are scoped to .px-int, the class carried on the body of internal pages only. The V3 alignment corrections that follow them edit base rules, but every selector they touch (.px-crumb, .px-ihero, .px-answer, .px-keys, .px-proc, .px-fact, .px-surf, .px-index, .px-cmp, .px-note, .px-areablock, .px-form) is absent from index.html, which was checked rather than assumed. The approved home page is untouched. Each correction answers a measured failure rather than a preference.

RefMeasuredCorrection
V6-1--aqua-ink measured 4.32 to 4.35 against the sky surface. AA needs 4.5.Darkened to #047A8B on internal pages. 4.58.
V6-2.px-band__p measured 4.35 at 390px over the photograph.The band scrim is deepened on the narrow layout only.
V6-3Two 500×500 client photographs upscale past 1.0x above 500 CSS pixels.Figures carrying one are capped at 500px and centred.
V6-5At 320px the chevron inside a wrapped CTA leaves the button box.The label and chevron are allowed to wrap together.
V6-8--slate measured 4.37 on the sky surface.Darkened to #577280 there. 4.62.
V6-9.px-band__p measured 4.45 over the brighter photographs at desktop widths.The two lightest stops of the band scrim are deepened from 601px up.
V6-10A long place name in the .px-answer__k label overflowed its 120px box at 390px.The label is allowed to break.

One v6 condition was found and deliberately left alone: the footer jumps from h2 to h4. It is not a WCAG AA failure, and correcting it would have made the shell differ from the approved design. It is recorded in the handoff as a CMS-side improvement instead.

Final client-ready correction pass

RefMeasuredCorrectionPages
F-01The home page before and after section said every pair was one of the client's own jobs, shot from the same spot. The four before files are named ...-before-SIMULATED-... and the register records them as generated, so the claim was untrue. The four after images are recorded as unverified, and all eight carried alt text asserting the work was Prime Exteriors'. A stat beside them read “100% — our own jobs, never stock”.The lede presents the pairs as illustrative comparisons and links to Our work for real photographs. All eight alt texts were rewritten: no “by Prime Exteriors”, and the before images no longer describe themselves as the same property photographed earlier. The stat now reads “Free — quoted from your photos”, which is true and is what the paragraph beside it already offers. Layout, images, slider behaviour, styling and section position are unchanged. Our work explains in one clause why the home page sliders are labelled as illustrations, so the two pages agree.2
F-02Thirteen headings stated a number that did not match what sat under them.All thirteen corrected, listed page by page on the start-here page. Where the number earned its place it was made right; where it added nothing the heading now reads naturally without one. On pool-surround-cleaning the fourth card asks the customer for something rather than stating what we do, so the heading was widened to cover both rather than the card being moved.13
F-03A sweep of every other heading and caption that states a number, checked against the rows, cards, steps or links beneath it: 253 of them. One more mismatch, on concrete-resurfacing, which claimed three answers above five.Corrected. The sweep ships as qa/countqa.py and runs every build. Headings whose number counts something the sentence names rather than the block beneath were read individually and left alone, which is most of them: “two systems” above eight rows comparing those two systems is a correct heading.1
F-04The ten client logos are all 800×400 files, but the artwork inside them fills anywhere from 20% to 96% of the canvas. Shown at one tile size, four of them rendered about a third the size of the rest and were illegible.Each logo is trimmed to its own artwork and re-centred in a common box, so all ten read at a comparable size. No artwork was altered, only the empty margin around it. The strip, the tiles and their styling are unchanged.1
F-05site.js still opened by naming home-v6.html as the approved source, and the design fingerprint register recorded v6 tokens and a v6 shell on all 149 rows.Both now name V7. Genuinely historical V6 references, in the change log and in the asset register notes, are left as they are, because they describe what was true at the time.150

One thing to settle before launch

The home page states $20m public liability cover. The verified business facts record no insurance certificate and list insurance under do not publish, so that figure is currently unsupported. It has been left in place rather than removed, because it is approved copy and taking out a trust signal is a commercial decision. Either supply the certificate or take the figure off. It is listed on the start-here page with the other items the client can close.

Everything from the earlier passes was re-checked and holds: the stacked answer block, centred table captions, call-out spacing in both adjacency orders, zero figcaptions, the three step form with V7 inline validation, the /thank-you/ route, the /service/, /commercial/ and /locations/vic/ hierarchy, and the global header component carrying the Quick Quote.

Integration and shared-component correction pass

home-v7.html is now the locked design reference. It was compared against the home page as built, and only the things that actually differ were taken from it: the hero photograph and its crop, and the inline validation messages. Everything else on the home page — colours, type, layout, cards, buttons, spacing, sections, the reviews and the star ratings — is unchanged, and every internal page still uses the same design system.

RefMeasuredCorrectionPages
V7-01The answer block ran a narrow key column beside the body, so its body copy began 192px right of the content edge and was the one block on the page not sitting on the grid every other block uses. That is what read as a misalignment. The reported cause was not the cause: the brief attributes it to later paragraphs flowing into the key column, and that was measured across all 143 blocks at 1920, 1440, 1180 and 999 before anything was changed. It never happens. Every block wraps its paragraphs correctly.The stacked treatment the component already used below 900px is now used at every width. The label keeps its rule, its case and its measure and sits above the copy; the copy starts on the content edge like everything else. The intentional stacking on tablet and mobile is unchanged.143
V7-02A call-out and a key row sitting directly together had nothing between them, in either order, so the two components ran into one another. Seven places sitewide, five of them call before keys and two the other way round.38px of separation set on the adjacency itself, so it applies wherever the two meet and nowhere else. No spacer elements and no page-specific margins.7
V7-03Visible captions sat under images on 106 pages.All 139 <figcaption> elements are gone and the CSS that styled them with them. 116 were descriptive captions and were removed outright. The other 23 were structural labels inside approved components — the gallery tile labels, the home page journey tags and the before and after headings — so those keep their text and their styling and only the element changed, which leaves the locked home page looking exactly as it did. All 803 alt attributes are untouched.106
V7-04The Quick Quote drawer was emitted on its own after the footer, which invites it being treated as page content. In a CMS that means editing every page to change it.The header, both navigations, the Quick Quote tab, the drawer, its form and its behaviour are now one component with one source, emitted as a single block above <main>. The handoff says plainly that it belongs in the global header template and not in page content, and sets out which part goes where.149
V7-07Homepage V7 arrived mid-pass and was compared against the home page as built. Two things actually differ: the hero photograph, which changes from the exposed aggregate driveway shot to a technician cleaning a paved courtyard, at 1800×1120 with fetchpriority="high"; and the validation, below.Both integrated. The hero crop is re-aimed to suit the new frame, and on a phone it moves up and left to hold the worker and the spray rather than empty sky. Nothing else on the home page changed: the reviews, the star ratings, the colours, the type, the cards, the buttons, the spacing and the section order are all as approved.1
V7-08Validation showed its message in the browser's own bubble, which disappears as soon as the field is touched and looks different in every browser.V7's inline messages are now the standard on every enquiry form: the message is written under the control, stays on screen while the field is being fixed, clears the moment it is right, and carries aria-invalid and aria-describedby. V7's wording is used as written. The one rule kept from this package rather than V7 is the phone check: V7 accepts any 8 to 15 digits, which passes 12345678, while this one accepts 0400 638 010, 0400638010, +61 400 638 010 and (03) 1234 5678 and rejects text. The three step system, the mandatory fields and the native final submission are unchanged.152
V7-09The closing band on the home page stretched a 1080px square client photograph across the full viewport width, which is why it looked soft. Four other images were greyscale, and read as damaged assets against the colour photography everywhere else.A wide version of the same scene was generated at 2752×1536 and sized to 1920 for the band. The client photograph is untouched and still used in the gallery, where it shows real completed work. The four greyscale images were regenerated in colour, same subject and framing, same file names. All five are recorded in research/image-asset-register.csv with their source and prompt.10
V7-05Table captions were left aligned.Centred once in the shared table styling. The table design, the header bar, the accessibility of the caption element and the mobile scroll behaviour with its sticky caption are all unchanged.60
V7-06Pages referenced their imagery from /uploads/, so importing a page meant uploading its assets first.Every image is embedded in the page that uses it as a Base64 data URI: 805 of them across 152 pages, all 66 assets accounted for, every string verified to decode to its declared type, and every image confirmed to render at 1440 and 390. Each is encoded as WebP at twice the largest box it is ever drawn in, so the size is paid where it buys sharpness and nowhere else.152

Embedding the imagery makes the package about eleven times larger

An embedded image is carried by every page that uses it instead of being downloaded once and cached across the site. The delivered HTML goes from about 11 MB to about 118 MB, and the home page from 121 KB to roughly 4 MB. Right-sizing and WebP already took 14.5 MB of source imagery down to 8.8 MB; the rest is repetition and cannot be compressed away.

On the live site that weight is paid on every page view by every visitor and it will show in Core Web Vitals on mobile. Embedding was chosen anyway, so that importing a page needs no asset upload. Once the site is in and the imagery sits in the media library, swapping the data URIs back to /uploads/ files is a find and replace per page and changes nothing else.

Preserved and re-checked after the shared changes: the breadcrumb margin:0 auto correction, the /service/, /commercial/ and /locations/{state}/... hierarchy, the three step form with every field mandatory, and the /thank-you/ success route.

Forms, URL structure and sitewide QA pass

Three jobs in one pass: collapse a mixture of form systems into one, put every service page under the singular /service/ root, and prove both with checks that drive the real pages rather than reading the source. No redesign, no content rewrite, no change to the approved home page visual direction or to its reviews.

One form system

RefWasIs
V6-25Three different forms. The slide-out panel had a three step form with eight fields. 144 pages carried a single step inline form with six. The home page hero had a third variant. A visitor could meet two of them on one page and be asked different questions.One component, rendered 293 times across 149 pages. Every enquiry point uses it: Get a Quote, Contact, the slide-out panel, the quote section on every service, commercial and location page, and all three positions on the home page. The panel template is now a single marker that pulls the same component in, so the form cannot drift apart again.
V6-26Fields were a mixture of required and optional, and the sub-copy said “fields marked * are required”.Every visible field is mandatory: ten required attributes per form. Step 1 Name, Phone, Email, Suburb. Step 2 Service, Property type, Rough size. Step 3 Message. Nothing was added that was not already being asked somewhere, and nothing optional was kept. The sub-copy now says why.
V6-27Validation was whatever the browser did with the attributes. A name of three spaces passed. A phone number of hello passed.Native constraint validation, extended through setCustomValidity() for the two rules the browser does not have: a value that is only whitespace, and the shape of an Australian number. 0400 638 010, 0400638010, +61 400 638 010 and (03) 1234 5678 are all accepted; brackets, dots, dashes and spaces are ignored before the check. Continue validates only the step on screen, shows the browser's own message, focuses the first invalid control and does not advance.
V6-28A required field in a step the visitor had not reached was still in the document, so the browser could refuse a submission over a field nobody could see and give no visible reason.Controls in an unreached step are disabled, which excludes them from validation and from submission both. Each step is enabled as it is reached, so at the Send button every control is enabled and carries its value. The final submission stays native: no preventDefault() on a valid submit, no fetch, no XHR, no AJAX, no custom submission logic. The one guard on Send fires only when an earlier step has gone invalid, and shows that step.
V6-29Get a Quote put the whole form in a narrow column beside its introduction, so the page's main purpose read as a sidebar widget.The introduction sits centred above a 780px form panel on its own, with the three steps as a row of cards rather than a vertical list. Contact uses the same arrangement, with the phone, email and hours block kept above the form so it is still the first thing found.
V6-30A successful submission returned to the Get a Quote page, which reads as though nothing was sent. The thank you page's own buttons reopened the quote panel on top of the confirmation.Every form declares data-success="/thank-you/", and the handoff tells the developer to set that redirect in the dashboard — the attribute documents the intent, the dashboard does the work. The page stays noindex, follow. A preview-only handler in site.js makes the flow testable from the folder; it is gated to localhost and labelled REMOVE BEFORE PUBLICATION.

One URL source of truth

RefWhat changedCount
V6-31Service pages moved from the plural /services/ to the singular /service/, hub included, with the parent and child hierarchy preserved. The live site already uses the singular root for the pages that rank: /service/driveway-cleaning/, /service/gutter-cleaning/ and /service/window-cleaning/ are live, indexed and carry ranking keywords, while /services/ is a live indexed hub with 107 words and no ranking keywords. So this is not a rename of the money pages; it is the hub moving to join them.52 service routes
V6-32Every link and every technical reference updated with it: navigation, footer, body links, breadcrumbs, canonical tags, Open Graph URLs, JSON-LD url and @id values, BreadcrumbList items, Service and WebPage nodes, the sitemap records, the route map and the handoff.0 remaining active /services/ references anywhere in the package
V6-33Because /services/ was live and indexed, a permanent redirect to /service/ is required and is in the redirect map. The previous map held the reverse of it, which would have sent the new hub back to the retired one. No destination in the map is also a source, so there are no chains and no self-redirects.6 redirects
V6-34Commercial routes verified under /commercial/ and location routes under /locations/{state}/{service-name}-{location}/, all lowercase and hyphen separated. Review files stay flat .html for the folder preview; production URLs are the hierarchical ones, and no site content links to a .html file.14 commercial, 67 location
V6-35The preview resolver in site.js used to be a hand-maintained list, so a URL change left it stale. It is now generated from route-map.csv on every build, and the build fails if any route has no review file. The route map is the single source of truth the brief asked for.149 routes, every target present

Found by looking, in the final page by page pass

Eight readers went through all 152 pages at desktop, tablet and mobile. Everything below was then re-measured before it was touched, which matters: three of the most alarming reports — a blank band at the foot of the home page and of the services page, and seven of the ten client logos missing — turned out to be failures of the screenshot run itself, not of the pages. They render correctly. Two more — a centred section heading sitting among left-aligned ones, and a hero fact row leaving a gap — are the approved design doing what it was built to do, and were left alone.

RefMeasuredCorrectionPages
V6-36The comparison table scrolls sideways below 720px (V6-15), but nothing said so. At 390px it hid 208px of itself behind a hard edge, usually cutting the last column mid word, and a phone visitor had no way to know the column was there. Every page carrying a table did this.The scroll is unchanged; the affordance is what was missing. A fade over the right edge shows the content continues, and a line under the table says to swipe. Both are drawn only while something is genuinely hidden, so a table that fits is untouched at every width, and both clear once the visitor reaches the end.60
V6-37The council count badge was drawn as a full width pale bar with its label stranded at the far left, rather than as a pill. This was caused by V6-17 in the previous pass: the flex basis that makes the badge take a line of its own was also setting its width.The badge still claims its own line and is then clamped back to the width of its own text. 112px instead of 548px.2
V6-38A hyphenated place name broke across two lines at the hyphen, so a heading read “…inside Merri–” over “bek with their own page”.The hyphen in a proper noun is part of the word, so headings now carry a non-breaking hyphen. It is applied to heading text only — never to a title, a meta description, a URL or anything in the JSON-LD — so nothing a machine reads is altered.7
V6-39Five photographs had a flat band baked into the file, not added by CSS. Two of them were severe: a dead grey strip down the left of a full width banner, 518px of a 1920px image on one and 470px on the other, so a quarter of the picture was blank. The other three carried a thin white frame around the edge, which read as a photo sitting in a box.The bands are cropped out of the files. File names are unchanged, so no markup moved. The two banners were scaled back to their original width afterwards, because the build refuses an image under 1800px for a full bleed backdrop.7
V6-40In the handoff and start-here pages the padding on an inline code chip pushed the following full stop away from it, so a sentence ending in a path read as “index.html .”Punctuation that follows a chip is pulled back against it.3

Two further things were found and are reported rather than changed, because the brief is explicit that this pass is not permission to rewrite approved copy. Both are listed in full on the start-here page. A heading on pool-surround-cleaning says “three things” above four cards; it is one of thirteen headings sitewide whose number does not match what sits under it. And several hero headings break with a single word on the second line. Hero headings are set to avoid that where the words allow, but a two word place name at the end of a line cannot always be helped without either splitting the place name, which is worse, or editing the heading.

How this was proved

The form checks drive the real form in a real browser. Fields are typed into, buttons are clicked, and what the page does next is read back — nothing inspects the source. Each of the §24 cases is performed on nine separate contexts: Get a Quote, Contact, the slide-out panel, a service page, a commercial page, a location page, the home page hero, the home page inline section and the thank you page panel.

  • Form behaviour. 279 assertions, all passing. Empty step holds and focuses Name. abc@, hello as a phone and a whitespace-only name all refuse to continue. All four Australian formats are accepted. Missing service, property type and size each hold the step. An empty message cannot submit. Going back preserves every value in both directions. Every control is enabled at the final step. A complete submission lands on the thank you page.
  • Sitewide form QA. 293 forms, every one the standard three step system, every visible field required, every success destination /thank-you/, no form carrying an action or a submit handler, no legacy single step markup anywhere.
  • Sitewide URL QA. All ten criteria clean: no retired path, no link outside the route map, no broken canonical, no wrong commercial or location route, no uppercase slug, no .html link in site content, no stale schema, canonical, Open Graph or breadcrumb destination.
  • Responsive form QA at desktop, tablet and mobile on every context, looked at rather than measured only.
  • The breadcrumb margin:0 auto fix and the tighter .px-answer key column from the previous pass are both preserved and re-measured after the form work landed.

The home page

The home page has been locked through every previous pass, and its visual direction, reviews and star ratings are unchanged here. Two things on it did change, because the brief named home page forms and home page sections as part of what had to be unified: all three of its forms now render the standard component, inside their existing panels with every container, colour, type style and panel treatment untouched; and 78 link paths moved from /services/ to /service/, verified by diff to be the only other change to the file.

V3 alignment and consistency pass

A later instruction asked for a focused alignment correction over the finished V3 build: fix the breadcrumb once in the shared stylesheet, rebalance the answer component, put every page on one content grid, then validate page by page at 1920, 1440, 1180, 820 and 390. No redesign, no content rewrite, no change to the approved architecture or to the locked home page.

The breadcrumb fault turned out to have a second instance. Both the breadcrumb wrapper and the interior hero carry .px-wrap and then set a shorthand padding with a zero horizontal value, which overrides the grid gutter. The breadcrumb also set margin:0, which overrides the centring. Below 1200px the hero fault put the heading, lede, buttons and figure of every internal page hard against the viewport edge.

RefMeasuredCorrectionPages
V6-11The breadcrumb wrapper began at the viewport edge: 384px left of the content edge at 1920, 144 at 1440, 24 at 1180 and 820, 18 at 390.margin:0 auto and padding:14px var(--gut), so the wrapper uses the same centred grid as everything else.148
V6-12The interior hero sat 24px wide of the content edge on both sides at desktop, and had no gutter at all at or below 1200px.The gutter is restored in all four of its padding declarations. The wide centred hero keeps its approved 980px measure by carrying the gutter outside it.148
V6-13The answer block used a proportional key column, so its body copy sat 260px inside the content edge at 1920 and 256px at 1180, drifting with the viewport.A fixed 160px key column with a 32px gap. The body now starts 192px in at every width, which is a predictable second grid line rather than a moving proportion. Letter spacing eased so no label breaks mid-word.144
V6-14A four item key row or process strip fell to three columns between 760 and 999px, leaving the fourth item alone beside an empty cell. 60 of 152 pages. A six item key row never fits across a 1152px column, so it stranded its sixth item at every desktop width.Quantity queries wrap four as two by two, five as three plus two, six as three plus three. A three item row is untouched, and a browser without :has() keeps the old layout.60
V6-15Below 720px the comparison table is given a 560px minimum and scrolls in its own box. Its caption was laid out at that same minimum, so at 390px the sentence ran off the visible area.The caption is pinned to the scroll origin and sized to the visible width.61
V6-16Suburb and Service share a row in equal halves. The longest service name needs 232px and the half was 196px, so a pre-selected value was cut off mid-word at 1920 and 1440.Service takes the larger share of the row above the stacking breakpoint.142
V6-17The council count badge is a flex item inside the region heading. On the one heading short enough to leave room it stayed on the first line, so that block ran 33px out of step with the block beside it all the way down.The badge always takes a line of its own.1
V6-18
V6-20
V6-21		In a key row, a card row and the child index, each item laid itself out independently. One heading wrapping to a second line pushed that item’s body copy 12 to 38px below its neighbours and the row read ragged.Subgrid puts every heading on one row and every description on the next. It costs nothing on a row where no heading wraps, which was measured before and after on a row of each kind.99
V6-24A link on a dark surface was lifted to the light aqua inside prose only, so an inline link in a key row kept the on-light colour and measured about 1.6 against the panel behind it.The lift covers every inline link on a dark or deep surface. Pixel measured afterwards: 0 failures.149
V6-23A two word place name was split across two lines of a hero heading, so a suburb read as “Box” over “Hill”. What was checked, and what was left alone

Every element carrying .px-wrap on all 152 delivered files was measured against the site grid at thirteen widths from 320 to 1920. The only boxes that do not sit on the 1200px grid are the 51 centred wide heroes, which are a deliberate exception and are centred to the pixel.

Three conditions were found and deliberately not changed, because they belong to the locked home page or to its design system:

  • The review cards on the home page let one card’s stars sit 15px below its neighbours’ when a reviewer name wraps. The same component is on the reviews page. Correcting it on internal pages only would make the two differ, so both keep the approved behaviour.
  • The home page photo mosaic is deliberately asymmetric, with one figure spanning two columns and two rows. It is excluded from the even-wrap rules.
  • The home page conditions already recorded above, the aqua ink contrast and the three images used slightly above 1.0x, are unchanged.

Thirteen headings and table captions state a count that does not match the rows or cards beneath them. They are listed in the handoff. They were not corrected, because this pass was explicitly not permission to rewrite copy, and in at least one case the right answer may be to move an item rather than change a number.

The script

site.js opens with the home-v6.html scripts verbatim, then appends the preview bootstrap required by section 23.9. That block is gated on the file: protocol and localhost, so it is inert on the real domain, and it is marked for removal before publication. It never calls preventDefault and never touches a form.

Phase sequencing override

V8.0 stops after the Phase 2 representative family for a checkpoint. The operator instruction of this build authorised continuing through the whole approved internal page scope in one pass, and that override is recorded here as section 3 of that instruction requires.

It changed sequencing only. Page QA, SEO ownership, anti-cannibalisation, anti-doorway rules, brand voice, factual accuracy, accessibility, link QA, image QA, responsive QA and the no-fabrication requirements were all applied to every page, and every page passed before the next was built.
